Project a Reference Fit's Predictor onto the Blocks That Did Not Match

Source: R/start.R
project_blocks.Rd

Estimates the coefficients of the blocks that the StartFrom method of start_at() left pending, which are terms that the two models share written on a different basis. The estimate is by least squares against the part of the reference's predictor that the blocks already carried across do not explain.

Usage

project_blocks(spec, design, ref, rdesign, out, pending)

Arguments

spec

The StatmodSpec() being started.

design

Its design.

ref

The reference StatmodFit().

rdesign

The reference's design.

out

The starting coefficients as they stand, with the matched blocks already written in.

pending

A list, one entry per distribution parameter, of list(nm, idx) pairs naming a block and the columns that it occupies.

Value

A list with start, the coefficients with the pending blocks estimated, and taken, a list of one-row-per-coefficient data frames recording what was projected.

Details

Two bases of the same term span different subspaces, so \(B_{\mathrm{new}}\beta_{\mathrm{new}} = B_{\mathrm{old}} \beta_{\mathrm{old}}\) has no solution in general, and the projection $$\hat\beta_S = \arg\min_\beta \lVert X_S\beta - r\rVert^2, \qquad r = \eta^{\mathrm{ref}} - \eta_{-S},$$ gives the closest reproduction of the fitted function that the new basis allows. Only the pending columns \(S\) are estimated. The vector \(r\) is the partial residual of the reference's predictor \(\eta^{\mathrm{ref}}\) after the blocks already matched by name are removed at the values that they were given (\(\eta_{-S}\) is the new model's predictor when the pending columns are set to zero). Both predictors are read through statmod_design_at(), so a block that moves with its coefficients (a break-point or a nonlinear term) contributes its value and not its linearization \(X\beta\). Where every block matched exactly there is nothing to solve, and a refit whose bases all agree returns the coefficients that it was given.

The projection is exact when the reference's function lies in the span of the new basis, and it reduces to the identity when the two bases coincide, so the name match above is a shortcut and not a different answer. Any part of the predictor that the reference explains and for which the new model has no column, such as a covariate that the formula dropped, stays in \(r\) and is absorbed by the pending blocks.

The two responses must be identical, so that the two designs are read at the same rows: the projection compares two predictors observation by observation and has no meaning across different data. Both models must be free of structural terms, whose contribution is the state of a recursion and not a function of the coefficients. Where either of these two conditions fails, the coefficients are returned unchanged. A pending block that itself moves with its coefficients (for example seg(x) refitted as seg(x, npsi = 2)) is not projected, because its coefficients are not those of a linear block, and it keeps the values given by the fallback strategy. The pending columns of an equation are also left to the fallback when their design has more than \(5 \times 10^7\) entries.

See also

start_from(), whose method calls it.
